Somewhere in the old lanes of Mumbai, a sweet aroma stops you in your tracks. It's coming from a Parsi kitchen and it's Dhansak.
In Parsi households, Dhansak is a dish of celebration laid out on Sunday afternoons. And the same dish, carried quietly, on days of mourning.
Few recipes hold so much of a community's heart.
The Parsis arrived in India in the 8th century and their elder famously added sugar to a bowl of milk, saying: "We will merge like sugar in this great land, and add only to its sweetness."
